23 A stationary sound wave is set up between a loudspeaker and a wall.
A microphone is connected to a cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO) and is moved along a line
directly between the loudspeaker and the wall. The amplitude of the trace on the CRO rises to a
maximum at a position X, falls to a minimum and then rises once again to a maximum at a
position Y.
The distance between X and Y is 33 cm. The speed of sound in air is 330 m s–1.
Which diagram could represent the CRO trace of the sound received at X?
A
B
1 cm

time base 0.50 ms / cm

hints: Notice X and Y are both positions of maximum CRO amplitude with one minimum between them - what points in a stationary wave are these and what is the separation X to Y in terms of wavelength?
Use the $33 \text{ cm}$ X to Y distance to find the full wavelength $\lambda$, then use $v = f\lambda$ with $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the sound frequency and period.
Convert the period to CRO horizontal divisions using time base $0.50 \text{ ms / cm}$ and compare with how many cm one full sine wave occupies in diagrams A to D.
walkthrough: X and Y are both maxima of detected amplitude with a minimum between, so they are adjacent antinodes of the stationary wave. Adjacent antinodes are $\lambda/2$ apart.
The progressive wave frequency is $f = v/\lambda = 330/0.66 = 500 \text{ Hz}$. The microphone at X detects this same frequency.
With time base $0.50 \text{ ms / cm}$, one period occupies $T/(0.50) = 2.0/0.50 = 4.0 \text{ cm}$ horizontally on the CRO.
Only the trace with one full sine wave every $4 \text{ cm}$, showing about two full waves across the $8 \text{ cm}$ screen, matches $T = 2.0 \text{ ms}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Shows about one oscillation in $3.0 \text{ ms}$, giving $f \approx 330 \text{ Hz}$, which is too low for $\lambda = 0.66 \text{ m}$ with $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: Shows a period of $2.0 \text{ ms}$ and so $f = 500 \text{ Hz}$, which matches $f = v/\lambda$ from the $33 \text{ cm}$ antinode separation.

C.explanation: Shows about one oscillation in $3.0 \text{ ms}$, giving $f \approx 330 \text{ Hz}$, which does not match the $500 \text{ Hz}$ required by the stationary wave spacing.

D.explanation: Shows about $2.5$ oscillations in $2.0 \text{ ms}$, giving $f \approx 1250 \text{ Hz}$, which is much too high for the calculated $500 \text{ Hz}$ wave.
